<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b1cdf9cbb74db8b70133c5d4e77cd9407702ff9e` — the merge of head `6d6e25955b97efa12e20fcd43072a68f41521eb1` into base `fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b1cdf9cbb74db8b70133c5d4e77cd9407702ff9e && git checkout b1cdf9cbb74db8b70133c5d4e77cd9407702ff9e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048 6d6e25955b97efa12e20fcd43072a68f41521eb1 && git checkout -B drift-repro fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048 && git merge --no-ff 6d6e25955b97efa12e20fcd43072a68f41521eb1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review (full) · REWORK** · Head-sha: `a65f6b41fb05abe4e28066790ebb4e98b63fb574` · card #34655 half B (`Refs #34655`) · read 2026-11-17T13:07Z

No earlier L1 record exists. L1-b2 read `0c7fc785` informally in a thread message. Inputs: card body; claim 6943786242 and half-B amendment 6944022372; dev reports 6946220643 and 6948138832; hand-off 6948282082; takeover 6948719649. Also the net diff from merge-base `07f2861f` (8 files, +256 / -14) and the check-runs on this head. I read everything on GitHub and in git at this head.

### Must-fix

**M1. On a name two packages hold, the toggle door's new read-back can report the other package's flow.** This is in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:4443-4447`. The `200` now answers `getFlowRuntimeStates().find((s) => s.name === name)`. The comment above it says "A name two packages hold never reaches here (`toggleFlow` refuses it), so the name's row is the flow switched". That holds for the bare engine entry. It does not hold for the slotted path, read in code at this head:

- **The slotted path reaches this handler.** A qualified address `/automation/:ns/:name/toggle`, and a bare name whose one served holder remains (#33386), are admitted as `status: 'slot'`. The door then swaps `automationService` for `flowSlotView(automationService, packageId, name)` (`automation.ts:4083-4088`).
- **The view's `toggleFlow` switches the right slot.** It goes through `slots.toggleFlowSlot` (`flow-slot-view.ts:167-168`).
- **The view does not bind `getFlowRuntimeStates`.** It is not among the members in `bound` (`flow-slot-view.ts:160-176`), so the proxy hands back the engine's own method.
- **The engine returns one row per slot, under the bare name.** `getFlowRuntimeStates` maps each slot key through `flowSlotName` (`flow-definitions.ts:266-276`, "two packages' flows of one name are two rows of that name").
- **So `.find` returns the first row of that name in `flows` order,** which belongs to whichever holder registered first, not necessarily the slot just switched.

Failure scenario, on the fixture of `packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-name-per-namespace.dogfood.test.ts` Q4: alpha's `qa_ns_q4` is switched off, and theta's `qa_ns_q4` is installed and on. `POST /automation/theta/qa_ns_q4/toggle {enabled: true}` switches theta's flow on (no change), then answers `200 {enabled: false}`, which is alpha's row. Theta's flow is on. That is the false toggle answer this card exists to remove, moved onto a path that answered correctly before: the echo was true there, and with this PR's refusal it is true by construction. I read this in code and did not run it. Pins on the slotted address would settle it.

Fix either way:
- read the switched slot's own row: bind a `getFlowRuntimeStates` (or a one-row read) in `flowSlotView` that answers the slot key's row;
- or keep the echo when the service is a slot view, which this PR's refusal makes true.

Either fix needs a door pin with two holders: toggle the holder registered second, and the answer must equal that slot's state, with a CONTROL on the first holder. Fix the comment at `:4440-4442` to match.

### Should-fix

**S1. The PR body carries a withdrawn routing line.** The body's `Contract-review-handoff: review#1 — CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER routed by maintainer order (…) · head a65f6b41…` line (its routing stamped 2026-11-17T12:31Z) names a review seat whose routing was withdrawn at 12:34Z (hand-off 6948282082 says the same of half A's body). The contract review now comes from seat 3. Remove or replace the line when the body is next edited. The card thread is gone, so the area edits the body.

### Checklist (the rest holds)

- **Shape:** Draft against `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`. The only card reference is `Refs #34655`, with no closing keyword. Half A's #34793 carries the `Fixes`. Title is `fix(automation)!`.
- **Scope vs claim:**
  - `flow-definitions.ts`, `runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, the tests beside them and `.changeset/` are in claim 6943786242.
  - `engine.ts` is in amendment 6944022372, which allows "two hunks only". The diff has exactly those two: the `toggleFlowKey` host literal gains `flowStatusDisabled`, and the `toggleFlow` docblock gains its `@throws` line.
  - The two existing tests edited (`flow-activation-ledger.test.ts` and `flow-activation-late-trigger.test.ts`) sit beside `flow-definitions.ts`, and the body names each with its reason.
- **The refusal** (`flow-definitions.ts:554-565`):
  - It sits after `refuseCustomerAuthoredToggle` and before `packagedFlowOwner` and the ledger write, so nothing is written or flipped.
  - It reads `flowStatusDisabled`, the verdict `registerFlow` records, so there is one source for the status rule.
  - It refuses only `enabled: true`, and its sentence names the step that arms the flow.
  - Its error shape `{ code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409 }` is the same as the provenance refusal's on the same door (`:563`).
  - The §7.3 subflow remedy still never prescribes the toggle (`flow-activation-ledger.test.ts`, `not.toContain("Enable 'shared_step'")`).
  - The other `toggleFlow` caller, `flow-slot-view.ts:168`, reaches the same body through `toggleFlowKey`, so the refusal also holds on the slotted path.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches the diff: one door answer moves from 200 to 409, and an `active: false` row is no longer overwritten. The card's Asked item B allows the refusal. `Metadata-protocol: none` with `patch` for `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/runtime` follows the level rule. `Check Changeset` is `success`. The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` holds: no key, value, type or stored row shape moves.
- **Changeset text,** read sentence by sentence: both moved paths and the one-line fix are stated. The "Unchanged" list matches the code, since toggle off still writes, `active`/`draft` behave as before and the provenance refusal comes first. One statement depends on M1: "The door's `200` answer reads `enabled` back from `getFlowRuntimeStates`, the same reading `GET /automation/_status` serves." Once M1 is fixed, re-read that sentence and the body's matching bullet against the fix.
- **Docs and skills:**
  - `Skills-docs: none` is true: `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:51` teaches only `{ enabled: false }`.
  - No page in `content/docs/**` states the toggle-on answer for a status-disarmed flow.
  - `ToggleFlowResponseSchema.enabled` ("New enabled state", `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts`) stays true once M1 is fixed.
- **Tests:** there are new pins in `toggle-door-packaged-only.test.ts` (obsolete and invalid refused; both ways; off accepted and held after an `active` republish; the arming step completes; CONTROLs `active` and `draft`) and in `automation-toggle-caller.test.ts` (read-back disagrees both ways; CONTROL; no-read echo). The ablation in the body turned 5 of 63 red (refusal) and 2 of 6 red (read-back), and the expected CONTROLs stayed green. No pin covers the slotted address, which is the M1 gap.
- **Narrowing evidence:** the body reports a full dogfood run on `a65f6b41fb` (479 files, 4059 tests, `VERDICT command-exit 0`), which is the current head.
- **Gates at this head:** 57 check-runs, all completed: `success` or `skipped`, none failed. The earlier `Live E2E UI` red (`studio-editor.spec.ts:74`) is `success` on its rerun. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`.

### Owed

- A fix round for M1 and S1 on the same branch, then an L1 delta read.
- **Seat L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`:** the face is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. No L2 record exists at any head.
- Not governed (per the area). The narrowing still goes to the seat as Tier H, as the body says. It lands after #34654, and half A (#34793) after it.
- Note, no change asked: the body still opens with seat 2's attribution lines and ends with seat 2's signed trailer.

## 席位核对

**L1 delta review · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `8eee7ddbe2a23e44308b063f322536818168e144` · card #34655 half B (`Fixes #34655`) · read 2026-11-17T15:04Z

This reviews the delta from L1 6948915409 (REWORK at `a65f6b41`: M1 and S1). Inputs:
- dev report 6951786536;
- the delta `a65f6b41..494da208` (3 files, +123 / -13), read line by line;
- the main merge `8eee7ddb`, which takes #34654;
- the PR body;
- check-runs on this head.

- **M1 is closed, by the echo route, and I accept that route.** The door now keeps `getFlowRuntimeStates()` rows under the name and reads one back only when exactly one row exists. With two or more rows, it echoes the request. That is the slotted case, where rows carry no slot key, so a view cannot find its own row. I checked that the echo is true for the engine's service. `toggleFlowSlot` and `toggleFlow` both reach `toggleFlowKey` and then `toggleFlow` with the slot key. `flowStatusDisabled` is keyed by that same key (`engine.ts:5697`), so the status refusal judges the switched slot.
  - A switch-on that is not refused clears `flowLedgerDisabled` for that slot. A switch-off adds it.
  - `isFlowEnabled` composes exactly those two (`engine.ts:6864`).
  - So a 200 means the slot reads what the request asked.

  Binding `getFlowRuntimeStates` in `flowSlotView` would need a new engine member outside the claimed surface. Not doing it was the right call for this card. The one-row read-back, which is the point of the change, is kept for every name one package holds.
- **The pins are real.** There are five door pins on a name two packages hold:
  - switched on at the second holder's address while the first is off;
  - switched off at the second holder's address while the first is on;
  - the bare name whose only served holder is the second one registered;
  - CONTROL: the first holder's own state;
  - CONTROL: a one-package name still answers its row, not the request.

  The first three would each have answered the first holder's row before the fix. The body reports the ablation 3 red / 62 green, and the real-stack Q4 probe went red without the fix (`enabled: false` against `true`). I did not re-run them.
- **Prose:** the route docblock, the handler comment and the changeset sentence now state when the answer is an echo and why it is true. The handler comment's old claim, "A name two packages hold never reaches here", is gone.
- **S1 is closed.** The withdrawn routing line is removed from the body.
- **Merge:** the net diff over the PR's 9 files from the merge-base to `494da208` is line-identical to main..`8eee7ddb`.
- **Surface:** the delta moves `automation.ts`, `automation-addressed-route.test.ts` and the changeset, all inside the claim.
- **Gates at this head:** latest attempt per check, 53 checks: `success` or `skipped`, none failed. The narrowing battery is pinned to this head: 479 files / 4067 tests, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

No new findings.

**Owed, for the seat:** a contract-review delta at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for `a65f6b41..494da208`, which is a narrowing. Please include the echo-route judgment. Re-run the battery if the head moves again. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8eee7ddbe2a23e44308b063f322536818168e144`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/toggle-door-packaged-only.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-activation-ledger.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-activation-late-trigger.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-toggle-caller.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-addressed-route.test.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-activation-projection.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-slot-view.ts, packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (the last five outside the diff: read, not reviewed)

**First contract review of this PR, so the whole PR, not a delta.** No earlier `## Contract review` record exists on PR #34810 (its four comments are the docs-drift bot, a flake note, L1 REWORK 6948915409 and L1 delta ACCEPT 6951880023) or on card #34655 for half B. The L2 records the card names (6946901031, 6947617913) are half A's, on #34793. Inputs: the card body and its 19 comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...8eee7ddb` (9 files, +366 / -14; merge-base e9f65a3b57), and the 57 check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, `toggleFlow(name, true)` on a packaged flow whose status is `obsolete` or `invalid`: narrowed from resolve to `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409. Right.** `flow-definitions.ts:554` reads `flowStatusDisabled.get(name)`, the verdict `registerFlow` writes at `engine.ts:5697`. It sits after `refuseCustomerAuthoredToggle` and before the subflow guard, the store write and the projection write, so nothing half-flips. The error shape is the one the provenance refusal already uses on this door, so no new code or name is published.
- **Accept-set, switch-off of such a flow: unchanged. Right.** The row records the installation's choice and holds after a later `active` republish; pinned.
- **Accept-set, `active` and `draft` flows: unchanged. Right.** Both CONTROLs pinned.
- **Stored state, the second moved path: an earlier `active: false` row is no longer overwritten by a refused switch-on. Right, and declared.** It follows from refusing before the write. The changeset states it with its one-line remedy.
- **Public surface, the door's 200 body: `enabled` is read back from `getFlowRuntimeStates` when the name has exactly one row, else the request is echoed. Right.** See ④ for the echo route. The body's shape (`ToggleFlowResponseSchema`) does not move.
- **Public surface, `AutomationEngine`:** no member added. `toggleFlowKey`'s host literal gains one field; the `toggleFlow` docblock gains its `@throws`. Right, and inside claim amendment 6944022372 (two hunks only).
- **No change to `packages/spec`.** Right for this card half: no schema key, value or type moves.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — present on the PR body and the changeset, and it matches the diff: one request that answered 200 now answers 409, and one row is no longer overwritten.

The changeset carries `patch` for `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/runtime`, the `!` title and a **BREAKING** paragraph with who moves and the one-line fix. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head (both attempts), and that conclusion is the level gate's verdict. The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` holds: nothing exists for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flags:** the fix-round report 6951786536 has `open_questions: []` and `security_findings: none`. Earlier reports (6946220643, 6948138832) list only process deviations (three small vitest runs outside the verify lock, throwaway and deleted), none of which touches the contract.
- **Out-of-scope finding in 6951786536** ("`GET /automation/_status` rows for a name two packages hold carry no package or slot key; not a card"): answered in ④ as N3. I disagree with "not a card".
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The read-back filters an in-memory projection the engine already holds; the refusal removes a ledger write.
- **Gates on this head:** 57 check-runs, every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed. Note for the approver: the CI matrix job `Dogfood Regression Gate (shard/3)` is `skipped` by the path filter, so the aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate: success` did not run the battery. The narrowing battery on this head is the dev's locked run recorded in 6951786536 (479 files / 4067 tests, `VERDICT command-exit 0`), which I did not re-run.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**The narrowing itself.** Read against the published spec on `main`:
- `automation-api.zod.ts:673-678` declares the 200 body's `enabled` as "New enabled state". On `main` the door echoed the request, so for a status-disarmed flow that declaration was false. The read-back and the refusal together make it true.
- `automation-api.zod.ts:30-36` and `contracts/automation-service.ts:1971-1977` declare the switch as the activation-ledger bit of a packaged flow, and the status as the author's switch. `isFlowEnabled` (`engine.ts:6864`) composes the two and neither overrides the other. A switch-on over a disarming status therefore never delivered "enabled"; no declared capability to make such a flow run is taken away.
- What the refusal does withdraw is narrow: clearing an earlier `active: false` row while the status still disarms the flow (pre-arming it for a later `active` release). The spec declares no such pre-arming, the card's Asked item B offers the refusal by name, the result fails closed (the flow stays off until switched on again), and the changeset states it as BREAKING with the fix. I accept it as a declared narrowing and name it here so the Tier H approver sees it. The other route the card allowed (accept the write, answer `enabled: false`) would have kept pre-arming; that choice is the maintainer's to confirm, not a defect.

**The echo route, judged explicitly: echoing is correct. I could not make the door answer a state that differs from what is stored.** Attempts, each read in the tree at this head:
- **Two or more rows implies a shared name.** `getFlowRuntimeStates` (`flow-definitions.ts:267-277`) emits one row per key of `flows`, named `flowSlotName(key)`. Two rows of one name are two slots of that name, so `FlowSlotTable.isShared` (`flow-slots.ts:113`) is true and the enabled reading goes through `FlowActivationProjection.hasShared`.
- **Switch-on that returns 200.** The status refusal ran on the slot key: `toggleFlowSlot` and the bare `toggleFlow` both end in `toggleFlowKey(key)`, and `flowStatusDisabled` is keyed by that key (`engine.ts:5697`; `moveFlowRecords` at `engine.ts:5289-5299` moves it when a key moves). Then `flowLedgerDisabled.delete(flowName, packageOwner)` sets the holder's own row to on, and `hasShared` lets the holder's own row decide. `packagedFlowOwner(key)` for a shared slot is the slot's own package (`engine.ts:6157-6160`), so the row written is the row read. `isFlowEnabled(key)` is true.
- **A package-less `active: false` row over a shared name.** This was my best candidate: under two holders the row is not deleted (`if (!shared)` at `flow-definitions.ts:630`) and it keeps every holder off that has no row of its own. But the switch-on writes the holder's own row, and `hasShared` checks that row first. Enabled is true. `flow-slots-per-package.test.ts:429-433` pins this on the real engine.
- **Switch-off that returns 200.** The holder's own row is set off; `hasShared` answers true; enabled is false.
- **The one-row read-back.** `toggleFlow` throws "not found" unless the switched key is in `flows`, so a name's single row is the switched flow's row. This holds through `flowSlotView` too (a lone served holder beside a disabled co-holder).
- **A stale or unowned row on an unshared name** (`FlowActivationProjection.has`, the `holder === undefined` and stale branches) can leave a flow off after an accepted switch-on. That is the one-row case, where the door reads back and answers `enabled: false`, which is the truth and which the card allows.
- **A service that is not the engine** has no slots; with no read method or no row it keeps the legacy echo, as the changeset says.
- **Not binding `getFlowRuntimeStates` in `flowSlotView` was the right call for this card.** The rows carry no slot key, so the view would need a new engine member, outside claim 6943786242 and its amendment. See N3 for the follow-up.

**Nits** (none affects correctness or the contract; each is left as a follow-up or accepted deviation, since a fix outside the prose faces moves the head):
- N1 (nit) — the published contract's prose lists one refusal. `contracts/automation-service.ts:1971-1977` and `automation-api.zod.ts:30-36` name only the customer-authored 409; the status 409 is named in the engine docblock and the route docblock only. Follow-up: add the sentence in half A (#34793), which already edits `packages/spec`.
- N2 (nit) — the invariant the echo rests on has no pin on the real engine. The five door pins use an engine double whose `toggleFlowSlot` always sets the state, and the new refusal pins use names one package holds. Nothing committed asserts that `toggleFlowSlot(pkg, name, true)` on a status-disarmed co-held slot is refused. It holds today by the reading above (and the body's real-stack probe was throwaway). Follow-up card: one case in `toggle-door-packaged-only.test.ts` or `flow-slots-per-package.test.ts`.
- N3 (nit) — `GET /automation/_status` rows of a co-held name carry no package, which is why the door cannot read back there and why an administrator cannot tell the two rows apart. The dev noted it and filed nothing. It deserves a card: with a package on the row, the door reads back on every path and the echo goes away.
- N4 (nit) — in the echo case only, a definition republished `obsolete` between the refusal check and the return (the body awaits the run stores and the ledger write) would answer `enabled: true` over a flow now off.
